ORDER LIST: 607 U.S. — the orders of the Supreme Court of the United States for Monday, 6 October 2025. Thirty-nine pages. The studio added nothing to it and took nothing out.

Your screen is narrower than the sheet, so the sheet is here twice: whole and too small to read, then at four pixels to the millimetre, wider than the screen and moving sideways. What we counted

In the section headed CERTIORARI DENIED this document disposes of 820 petitions. 789 of them are disposed of by the one sentence on sheet 32 — eight words under a column of names. The remaining 31 are answered one at a time, in sentences, in the sheets that follow. We counted this ourselves from the source file, with the tooling committed beside the work; the count was published wrong for four sessions and corrected in the record.

The same strip, reduced to fit the width of your screen: all 8,424 pixels of it at once, at whatever scale your screen makes of them. Sheet 32 is 6,696–6,912 mm from the left-hand end and its sentence falls at 6,757.75–6,860.75 mm. Nothing marks it. (The instruction's figure of 8,420.1 mm is the nominal sheet at 215.9 mm; the render measures 216.0.)

This page is not the work. The work is the instruction below, and no one has mounted it. Nine readers have sat with sampled sheets of this document; none has sat with this page, and nobody has walked the wall. A strip you drag with a thumb is not 8.42 metres met by a body, and nothing here is evidence that it is.

NO PART

A print-and-instruction work. This instruction is the whole of the studio's authorship; every mark in the work is the Court's. Ensemble, 27 July 2026.

The document

1.(ORDER LIST: 607 U.S.) — the order list of the Supreme Court of the United States for MONDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2025.
https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/courtorders/100625zor_5368.pdf
SHA-256 354c9ba8dbc6e5104a6a6b84ee53a91a6f8e5e87b2d900e8c26f4a67ef6ec652
2.39 pages, each 612 × 792 pt = 215.9 × 279.4 mm. Every text operation in the file is set at 10.02 pt = 3.53 mm — one size, thirty-nine pages, no exception. Every visible glyph is Lucida Sans Typewriter, in its regular, Bold and Oblique variants. (The file also invokes a fourth font once, on page 3, to set a single space; it prints no mark. Recorded because it is true, not because it matters.) A file with a different hash is a different document and this instruction does not cover it.

Printing

3.Print all 39 pages, one to a sheet, at 100 % on one plain uncoated white or near-white stock. No scaling, no fit-to-page, no cropping, no trim, no bleed, no mark added to any sheet.
4.Printers scale by default. Measure one printed sheet against 215.9 × 279.4 mm, and the type against 3.53 mm, before printing the other thirty-eight.
5.Repair nothing and correct nothing. Whatever the file prints, the wall carries.

Mounting

6.Sheet 1 at the left-hand end; each sheet followed by the sheet with the next printed folio. The sequence is never reversed, reordered, doubled, or interrupted by anything but a break.
7.One sheet tall, everywhere. No sheet above or below another. The document is not to be re-stacked into a block.
8.0 mm joint. Within a run, adjacent sheets touch along their vertical edges — no gap, no overlap, no spacer, no batten. Between runs no distance is specified.
9.One height. The horizontal centre line of every sheet 1600 mm above the finished floor (bottom edge 1460 mm), level, the same in every run.
10.Every sheet flat against its wall and in one plane: not bent round a corner, not tilted, not framed, not matted, not glazed.
11.Nothing else on the wall or in the room: no label, title, date, credit, caption, arrow, floor mark, rope or vitrine, and no light aimed at one part of the run rather than at all of it.

The break

The line is 8,420.1 mm long. Almost no wall takes it. Where it breaks is yours.

12.A break falls between two sheets, never through one; runs are whole numbers of sheets, 215.9 mm each. The runs follow one another in order along the path a body walks.
13.Decide the break from the wall. Measure the room and let the sheets fall where they fall. Do not read the sheets in order to choose where to cut.
14.Forbidden: breaking at a heading, a section, or any boundary in the text; placing a chosen sheet at the start or end of a run, or keeping it away from one; giving any sheet a wall of its own; adjusting the joint, the height or the scale so a run comes out even.
15.Whichever break you choose, named people fall at it — round a corner, onto a return, behind the swing of a door, into a passage someone has to decide to enter. That is your decision, it is public, and it stands until the work comes down. Neither the document nor this instruction tells you who they are.

The approach

16.Site the work so that the room delivers a body to the sheet-39 end: the first part of the run a person entering comes within reading distance of is the free end of the last run, at sheet 39. The sheet-1 end is the closed end — an inside corner, the end of a wall, a dead end — with no route that brings anyone there first.
17.Do this with the room and nothing else. Nothing may be added anywhere to steer a person, and nobody is told which way to walk.
18.A wall has two ends. This makes the direction likely, not certain. Someone will walk it from sheet 1 and see the work in the other order, and we accept that rather than mark a floor.

If the wall is too small

19.If the longest single run carries fewer than 16 sheets (3,454.4 mm), mount it anyway and record that it did so. The work stands; what stops is us — no claim about what a body finds in that room may be made from that mounting.

What comes back

20.The date, the room, the number of runs, each run's length in sheets, the sheet numbers either side of every break, the height as built, which end of the line the way in reaches first and whether the room allowed a choice, and a photograph you made of what is on the wall. That record is the only evidence this work will ever have, and it is not ours to compose.

The hash, the page count, the page dimensions and the type in items 1 and 2 are measured first-hand on that file; everything else on this page is instruction and judgement and asserts no fact about the world. The work carries no text of its own — this page is not mounted, and there is no wall label.
